graphs.description: What the AdventureWorks OLTP sample means: people, customers, employees, sales and purchase orders, products, manufacturing, and inventory. Concepts bind to the pinned ModelSpec; shared concepts reuse the pinned core graph.
graphs.title: AdventureWorks OLTP

graphs.description: What the Chinook sample database means: a digital music store that sells tracks to customers in 24 countries. Each concept is bound to the ModelSpec record type or field that holds it; concepts that are not specific to Chinook are reused from the core concepts.
graphs.title: Chinook music store

graphs.description: Universal concepts that are not specific to any dataset (country, currency, customer, invoice, price, revenue, date, population, per capita and more), plus the meaning/draft-1 schema and format reference. Dataset graphs reuse them by address and pin a commit.
graphs.title: MeaningGraph core concepts

graphs.description: What the Countries reference database means: countries and territories keyed by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code with their alpha-3 code, currency and dated World Bank population, and aliases that map other datasets' country spellings to them. Concepts bind to the pinned ModelSpec model and extend the core country, country-code and population concepts.
graphs.title: Countries reference database

graphs.description: Preparatory source meanings for native time, currency and rate strings from the ECB daily XML resource. Reference date has no publication instant; the indicative rate expresses quote-currency units per one EUR with lexical digits preserved. No stable cross-read identity, synthetic EUR row, reciprocal, historical lookup or accepted country/tender/transaction join is asserted. CC0 covers authored metadata only; ECB rate reuse terms remain separate. Source execution and paid applicability stay blocked.
graphs.title: ECB daily euro foreign exchange reference quotes

graphs.description: What the Employees browser edition means: selected employee identities, departments, dated assignments, title histories, and salary histories from the upstream MySQL Employees sample. Concepts bind to the pinned ModelSpec and retain the source's CC BY-SA attribution and share-alike terms.
graphs.title: Employees (browser edition)

graphs.description: Source-qualified GeoNames countries, places, admin1 and alternate names, retaining native keys, historic country rows and unresolved references. Auxiliary demo country bridges preserve separate source property scopes; their target bindings alone do not authorize raw-label interoperability. Model and meaning metadata are CC0-1.0; source GeoNames data is CC-BY-4.0.
graphs.title: GeoNames source projection

graphs.description: What the Northwind sample business database means: customers place orders for products supplied and shipped by Northwind. Concepts bind to ModelSpec record types and fields; shared concepts reuse the pinned core graph.
graphs.title: Northwind small-business database

graphs.description: What the classic Pubs sample database means: authors write publications, publishers manage titles and employees, and stores record sales. Concepts bind to the pinned ModelSpec model, with reusable people, organization, employee, and price concepts from the core graph.
graphs.title: Microsoft Pubs publishing database

graphs.description: Accepted public source roles for the complete ROR schema 2 organizations recordset, retaining native URL identity, all statuses and ordered location and relationship projections. Source bindings do not authorize user field mappings or name-to-identity matching. Model and meaning metadata are CC0-1.0; embedded GeoNames data remains CC-BY-4.0 under the provider attribution.
graphs.title: Research Organization Registry source projection

graphs.description: The meaning of the MySQL Sakila sample database: films, actors, customers, rentals, payments and stores. Dataset concepts reuse pinned universal concepts from the MeaningGraph core.
graphs.title: Sakila video rental database

models.description: The ModelSpec for Microsoft's AdventureWorks OLTP sample, derived from the pinned SQL Server 2025 sample installer fixture. It describes the source tables and fields as a reusable model for copies of this database.
models.title: AdventureWorks OLTP

models.description: The data model of the Chinook sample database: a digital music store with artists, albums, tracks, playlists, customers, employees and invoices, as 11 record types whose names are the upstream table and column names. Anything that stores Chinook, such as a SQLite file, a CSV export or an OpenVaultDB database, is a copy of this model.
models.title: Chinook music store

models.description: Preparatory model of ECB daily XML decoder output: FxReferenceQuote retains native required time, currency and rate strings and declares no stable key. EUR base and indicative-reference kind are source-definition context, without an invented base field or EUR quote row. Date/currency grain is scoped to one returned response; observation identities distinguish republications. Decimal digits and trailing zeros remain lexical. CC0 covers authored model metadata only; source execution, retention and paid applicability are not admitted.
models.title: ECB daily native reference quote model

models.description: The ModelSpec for a reproducible browser-sized edition of the MySQL Employees sample. It describes the six native tables and their declared primary and composite keys without inventing identities.
models.title: Employees (browser edition)

models.description: Source-faithful model for four logical GeoNames recordsets: countries, places, admin1 and alternate names. Native text fields, keys and unresolved references remain available; auxiliary demo country bridge entities retain separate source property scopes. Model metadata is CC0-1.0; source data is CC-BY-4.0. Registration alone does not authorize raw-label interoperability.
models.title: GeoNames source projection

models.description: The data model of the classic Northwind sample database: customers, employees, orders, products, suppliers and related tables. Its record types and fields describe the pinned upstream SQLite schema; any copy of Northwind uses this model.
models.title: Northwind small-business database

models.description: The classic Microsoft Pubs sample model covers authors, publications, publishers, stores, sales and employees. It preserves all 11 native tables, including keyless discounts and royalty schedules without fabricated identity.
models.title: Pubs publishing database

models.description: Source-faithful ROR schema 2 model: organizations preserve native URL identity, status and original JSON; locations and relationships retain source array ordinals as physical projections of one logical organizations recordset. Model metadata is CC0-1.0; embedded GeoNames data remains CC-BY-4.0 under the provider attribution. Registration does not authorize a user identifier mapping.
models.title: Research Organization Registry source projection

models.description: The MySQL Sakila sample model for films, actors, customers, rentals, payments, stores and staff, represented by its 16 native table record types.
models.title: Sakila video rental sample
